blocks.text: ﷺ had taught them aspects of the Deen (and they were departing), some of them asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! We have no food for the journey." Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed Hadhrat Umar (RA) to supply them with some provisions, but he submitted, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I have nothing but some left-over dates which I do not think will be of any benefit to them." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Go and give them some provisions." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then took the people to an upstairs room where there were dates that resembled a little brown calf (in colour and height). Hadhrat Umar (RA) told the people to help themselves and each of them took as much as they needed. Hadhrat Nu'maan (RA) says, "I was the last of the lot and when I looked (at the dates), I could not see a single date missing (from the original heap) although four hundred people had already taken from it." (The dates did not diminish because of the blessings of complying with the order of Rasulullaah ﷺ).[^1]
The Incident of Hadhrat Dhukayn bin Sa'eed Khath'ami (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Dhukayn bin Sa'eed Khath'ami (RA) reports that they were four hundred and forty people who approached Rasulullaah ﷺ for food. Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed Hadhrat Umar (RA) to give them some food, but he submitted, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I have only that much which would suffice for my children and I during the four months of summer (it would not be enough for these people)." Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated the instruction and Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I hear and obey you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" Hadhrat Umar (RA) left with the people and took them to an upstairs room where he took out the key from his waist string and opened the door. In the room there was a heap of dates that resembled a baby camel that was sitting down. Hadhrat Umar (RA) told the people to help themselves and each of them took as much as they needed. Hadhrat Dhukayn (RA) says, "I was the last of the lot and when I looked (at the dates), it appeared as if we had not reduced the number of dates at all."[^2]

Hadhrat Dhukayn (RA) says, "We were four hundred people when we asked Rasulullaah ﷺ for food." The narration is then that same as the above narration but with the difference that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said (to Rasulullaah ﷺ), "I have nothing besides a few Saa of dates that would suffice only for my children and I during the four months of summer." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said to him, "Listen and obey." Hadhrat Umar (RA) responded by saying, "I hear and I obey."[^3]
Ahmad, narrating from reliable sources, as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.304). Tabraani has also reported the narration.
Tabraani, narrating from reliable sources, as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.304). Abu Dawood has reported a part of this narration.
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.365). Abu Nu'aym says that the narration is authentic and proves that Rasulullaah ﷺ was truly a prophet of Allaah.
